review: rebuilt a second time 2026-11-12 by Claude Fable 5.2 from the questionnaire answers, lexicon and visible paradigms, after the rule book was redecided natively with schedule reads and blind fluency reads of the rows; every held-out row passed on the first judged run. Audited adversarially 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 (renderer against the answers, some 2,900 renders against independently computed fire times, every row re-read): six sentence forms that said another schedule or contradicted themselves and four that could not be held were repaired test-first, and the four rules the builder had read loosely were decided in the answers; the new and changed sentence forms have not had a blind fluency read. Repaired a second time 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 with the core's calendar and set facts, the cross-language trap list and the usage notes (usage.md): a schedule that never fires and one that fires only in leap years now say so, open and holed year sets and long stepped sets are said as series, neither side of a date-or-weekday pair is an exception, Monday to Friday and Saturday and Sunday are named as days, and the rule book records where it departs from the usage notes; none of the forms of this round has had a blind fluency read either; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-13: length-gate work by Claude Opus 5.5: a nearest weekday beside Monday to Friday is not said, and every second of a minute after a time that needs no pin has no bracket; three shorter seconds forms were withdrawn after a blind native read found second readings; lists and stretches of seconds keep their brackets of example times, for the misreadings the rule book records; 2026-11-13: one place inside the hour or the minute is counted from its start («щогодини через 5 хвилин після початку години») instead of an ordinal pinned by clock times in brackets, by Claude Opus 5.5, after a blind native reader preferred the count for one value and the bracketed ordinal for a list; lists stay ordinals and are recorded as open; 2026-11-14: on the maintainer's rulings, by Claude Opus 5.5: a cadence of hours that tiles the day from midnight with three values or more is said bare («кожні 2 години», «кожні 6 годин»), one that tiles it from a later start names only its start («кожні 2 години, починаючи з 1:00»), neither takes «щодня» or a window, a minute or a second beside them is said as beside «щогодини», and hours taken out of them follow as an exception; every bracket of clock times or stretches (the pin's second form) is gone, and the Quartz note always follows the time; the rule book was amended first, the rows were rewritten by hand before the renderer changed, and nothing was blind-read; 2026-11-14, a second ruling the same day, by Claude Opus 5.5: no minute or second position is said as an ordinal any more («на 30-й хвилині» is read as the minute that ends at :30, a real off-by-one, not a reader's taste): lists are counts from the start of the hour or the minute said once («щогодини через 15 та 45 хвилин після початку години», minute 0 as «рівно й …»), runs and restarting cadences not from the start are «з 10 до 40 хвилин після початку кожної години», those from the start are durations («протягом перших 57 хвилин»), places left out are «крім моменту через 29 хвилин після початку кожної години», and a second beside several minutes follows after «щоразу»; rule book first, rows by hand before the renderer, nothing blind-read; 2026-11-14, a third ruling the same day, by Claude Opus 5.5: every other hour under a finer field is said by its parity («щохвилини в парні години», «кожні 15 хвилин у непарні години», «…кожної парної години»), longer steps keep «щоразу … протягом години»; a run of weekdays is «з понеділка по п'ятницю», with no «щотижня», no «включно» and no comma after it, since the rule book recorded no misreading behind the old form; rule book first, rows by hand before the renderer, nothing blind-read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 685 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (5046 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 16 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs); 2026-11-20, by Claude Opus 5.5: the same minutes in three or more hours, listed or a cadence of hours that does not tile the day, are said once, with the hours named once after «після» («щодня кожні 15 хвилин протягом години після 1:00, 4:00, 9:00, 14:00 та 18:00»; past five, a cadence is its first three hours «і так далі до» its last), in place of a window per hour, minutes fused into a rhythm's ends, or two rhythms stacked with «щоразу»; rule book first, rows by hand before the renderer; the 24 new and changed rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers briefed only in Ukrainian (214 questions each): no answer wrong
